title: Lean-Verified 81/29 Upper Bound for Tuza’s 1981 Triangle-Cover Conjecture
whyItMatters: AI research agents proved and formally verified in Lean 4 that every graph satisfies τ(G) ≤ (81/29)ν(G), lowering the 45-year-old Tuza conjecture bound below Haxell (1999) and Wang (Sept 2026) with dual-kernel checks.
summary: Registered on the Palomar Lean registry on November 22, 2026 (github.com/mathdiscoveries/tuza-triangle-cover), autonomous AI research agents built and directed by Tyler B. Hughes proved and formalized in Lean 4 that every finite simple graph G satisfies τ(G) ≤ (81/29)ν(G) ≈ 2.793 ν(G), where ν(G) is the maximum size of an edge-disjoint triangle packing and τ(G) is the minimum edge-cover of all triangles. Tuza conjectured τ(G) ≤ 2ν(G) in 1981 (Erdős Problem #167), and the general bound stood at Haxell’s 66/23 ≈ 2.870 for 27 years before falling to 63/22 (Aug 2026), Sichen Wang’s 165/59 ≈ 2.797 (Sept 2026), and now 81/29. Extending Wang’s MIT-licensed tuza-lean library with helper-arborescence coupling, unmerged coloured-family covers, and opposite-edge elimination, the 101-line Mathlib-only Challenge statement passed Palomar replay across two independent kernels (nanoda and con-ron) under Lean 4.35.0.
technicalHighlights: Lowers the general upper bound on Tuza’s 1981 triangle-cover conjecture (Erdős #167) to 81/29 ≈ 2.793, beating Haxell (66/23) and Wang (165/59).
Compact 101-line Mathlib-only Challenge statement includes explicit K4 non-vacuity checks (ν(K4) = 1, τ(K4) = 2) and dual-kernel Palomar verification (nanoda + con-ron).
Introduces helper-arborescence coupling and opposite-edge elimination discovered by autonomous AI agents.
caveats: No human mathematician has yet refereed the written exposition, and the specific underlying foundation models powering Hughes’s mathdiscoveries.org agent harness are undisclosed.

scoreRationale.foundational: Advances a well-known 45-year-old extremal graph theory conjecture (Erdős #167), though the full τ ≤ 2ν bound remains open.
scoreRationale.ripple: Extends reusable Lean 4 extremal-combinatorics machinery and demonstrates independent researchers running autonomous discovery agents.
scoreRationale.verification: Dual-kernel Palomar verification (nanoda and con-ron) against a short, auditable Mathlib-only statement with non-vacuity checks.
scoreRationale.velocity: Pushed past a 27-year barrier and improved upon a September 2026 bound within two months.
